module_title: Metallic and Non-Metallic Minerals - Basic Understanding
introduction: Minerals are naturally occurring substances with a definable internal chemical structure. In India, for industrial and geographical studies, minerals are broadly classified into two main categories: Metallic (containing metals) and Non-Metallic (devoid of metals).

core_concepts.title: Metallic Minerals
core_concepts.description: These minerals contain metal in raw form. They are generally hard, have a shine (luster), and can be melted to form new products. Examples: Iron ore, Copper, Gold, Silver.

core_concepts.title: Ferrous vs. Non-Ferrous
core_concepts.description: Metallic minerals are further divided into two types: 1. Ferrous (containing iron, e.g., Iron ore, Manganese, Nickel). 2. Non-Ferrous (not containing iron, e.g., Copper, Lead, Bauxite, Gold).

core_concepts.title: Non-Metallic Minerals
core_concepts.description: These minerals do not contain extractable metals. They are generally brittle and break when hit. Examples: Mica, Salt, Potash, Sulfur, Limestone, and Coal.

core_concepts.title: Iron Ore
core_concepts.description: It is the basic mineral and the backbone of industrial development. India is richly endowed with high-quality iron ore. 'Odisha' is the largest producer of iron ore in India.

important_entities.name: Bauxite
important_entities.significance: Aluminum is not mined directly from the earth. It is extracted from a clay-like substance called 'Bauxite'. Aluminum is highly valued because it combines the strength of iron with extreme lightness. 'Odisha' is the largest producer of Bauxite.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Students often get confused about where Coal and Petroleum fit. Remember, they are classified as 'Energy Minerals', but structurally, they fall under the 'Non-Metallic' category because they contain no metals.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Iron Ore, Bauxite, Manganese. Odisha is the leading producer of all three of these highly crucial industrial minerals.

exam_strategy_tips: Classification questions are very common: 'Which of the following is NOT a ferrous mineral?' (Look for Bauxite or Copper in the options).
The question 'Bauxite is an ore of which metal?' is a staple in basic GK exams. Answer: Aluminum.
